parts.text: Fig. 7.1 shows a barrier at the entrance to a car park. The wooden barrier arm has a weight of 60 N which acts through the centre of gravity at the position shown on Fig. 7.1. Fig. 7.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Initially the wooden barrier arm is horizontal.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Using Fig. 7.1, calculate the clockwise moment of the weight of the wooden arm about the pivot. clockwise moment = ................................................... Nm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The wooden barrier arm is in equilibrium. The mass of the soft iron bar A is 23 kg. Calculate the distance d between the pivot and the joint holding the soft iron bar A. distance d = ......................................................... [3]

ms.label: 7(a)(ii)
ms.text:
0.44 m OR 0.45 m
total clockwise moment = total anticlockwise moment
(d =) 100 / 225 OR (d =) 100 / (23 × 9.8) OR 100 / (23 × g × d)

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Fig. 7.2 shows a coil attached to a power supply placed below the soft iron bar A. Fig. 7.2

ms.label: 7(b)(i)
ms.text:
(barrier arm) rotates anticlockwise OR (RHS of barrier arm) moves upwards
(when the switch is closed) coil produces a magnetic field OR coil / core becomes an (electro)magnet
(coil/core/electromagnet) attracts (iron) bar (downwards)

ms.label: 7(b)(ii)
ms.text:
statement: (barrier arm) moves slower / goes up (more) slowly
explanation: decreases strength of (magnetic) field / smaller force / smaller moment

ms.label: 7(b)(iii)
ms.text:
steel would become permanently magnetised
(so when switch is opened) barrier would stay up or bar A will stay attracted (to soft iron core)
